content: 1. By law, it is illegal to charge for certain services. Did you have to pay for the services provided at this facility today? If so, how much did you pay, and for what specific services? Please indicate all applicable options: a. General service fee b. Blood tests c. Medicines or treatments provided d. Contraceptive methods (e.g., condoms, implants, IUDs) e. Do not know 2. Are you currently pregnant? Have you ever used a modern method of contraception in the past, such as oral contraceptive pills, injections, intrauterine devices (IUDs), or implants, but stopped using them? If yes, what methods have you used previously? Please indicate all applicable options: a. Lactational amenorrhea b. Natural methods (e.g., standard days, basal body temperature) c. Condoms (male or female) d. Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) e. Contraceptive injections f. Intrauterine devices (IUDs) g. Contraceptive implants 3. Why did you stop using modern contraceptive methods? Please indicate all applicable reasons: a. Stopped the method to become pregnant b. Became unintentionally pregnant while using the method c. Rarely having sexual intercourse d. Religious reasons e. Not allowed by partner or family f. Difficulty accessing the method g. Out of stock at the health facility h. Cost was too high i. Inconvenient to use j. Never informed about available options 4. Why have you never used a modern method of contraception? Please indicate all applicable reasons: a. Fear of side effects or health problems b. Rarely having sexual intercourse c. Religious reasons d. Not allowed by partner or family e. Difficulty accessing the method f. Out of stock at the health facility g. Cost was too high h. Inconvenient to use i. Never informed about available options 5. Do you have any fears or concerns about using a modern contraceptive method? If yes, what are they? Please indicate all applicable concerns: a. Bleeding between periods b. Irregular periods c. Mood changes d. Fear of not being able to conceive later e. Difficulty using the method regularly at home f. Difficulty obtaining resupply or doses 6. When was the last time a healthcare worker discussed contraception, family planning, or birth control with you? If never, skip to the next question. If yes, when? a. Today b. Within the past month c. More than a month ago (within the past year) d. More than a year ago 7. During the last visit when contraception, family planning, or birth control was discussed, did the healthcare worker: a. Ask whether you wanted to avoid getting pregnant? b. Ask whether you were at risk of getting pregnant? c. Ask whether you were using a method of contraception? d. Discuss any of the following methods of contraception: i. Pills ii. Contraceptive injections iii. IUDs iv. Implants v. Sterilization e. For any modern method (e.g., pills, injections, IUDs, implants, sterilization), did they: i. Discuss whether the method protects against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)? ii. Discuss the risk of pregnancy while using the method? iii. Address any concerns or fears you had about using the method? iv. Address your health concerns or fears? v. Recommend that you use a modern method? vi. Specifically explain the advantages of long-acting reversible modern methods (e.g., IUDs, implants)? 8. Were you given or prescribed a modern contraceptive method today? If no, skip to the next question. If yes, which method were you given or prescribed? a. Lactational amenorrhea b. Natural methods (e.g., standard days, basal body temperature) c. Condoms (male or female) d. Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) e. Contraceptive injections f. Intrauterine devices (IUDs) g. Contraceptive implants 9. Do you feel confident using the modern method you were given or prescribed today? Do you know where to obtain long-acting reversible methods (e.g., IUDs, implants)? If no, skip to the next question. If yes: a. How long does it take you to travel to obtain the method? b. Would the travel time affect your decision to use it? c. What is the cost of the method(s)? d. Would the cost affect your decision to use it? 10. Do you know where to obtain permanent methods such as bilateral tubal ligation (tying tubes) or male vasectomy? If no, skip to the next question. If yes: a. How long would it take to travel to get the procedure? b. Would the travel time affect your decision to use it? c. What is the cost of the method(s)? d. Would the cost affect your decision to use it? 11. Do you know where to go to obtain a termination of pregnancy (abortion)? Have you ever had a termination of pregnancy? Have you ever wanted an abortion but were unable to obtain one? If no, skip to the next question. If yes, why were you unable to obtain an abortion? Please indicate all applicable reasons: a. Did not know where to go b. Too expensive c. Afraid of complications or side effects d. Not allowed by partner or family e. Facility was unable to provide the service f. Did not trust the facility to provide the service g. Not allowed by law (illegal) 12. Did you have to pay for the service at this facility today? If yes, for what did you pay? Please indicate all applicable options: a. General service fee b. Blood tests c. Medicines or treatments provided d. Contraceptive methods (e.g., condoms, implants, IUDs) e. Do not know 13. Is the woman currently using a modern method of contraception? If no, skip to the next question. If yes, were any of the following recorded: a. Current contraceptive method being used? b. Presence or absence of problems with the current method? c. Presence or absence of side effects from the current method? d. Woman’s risk of STIs? e. Presence or absence of contraindications to the current method? f. Prescription given for the current method or a new method? g. Any follow-up visit for family planning? 14. If the woman is not using a modern method of contraception, were any of the following recorded: a. Reasons why a more effective modern method is not being used? b. Advice provided on the need to shift to a more effective method? c. Is the woman currently using only a traditional method of contraception or no contraception? 15. Review the availability of essential medicines, equipment, and supplies for family planning at outpatient clinics. This includes direct observation and consultation with staff familiar with the inventory. Ensure that stock records are available and up-to-date. 16. Review facility policies, guidelines, and standards for family planning services. Verify whether staff have been oriented on and use written policies, standards, or guidelines. Ensure that national protocols for contraceptive methods are followed, including risks, benefits, side effects, contraindications, and instructions for use.
